LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD is a font packaging file for Microsoft Windows 11 TrueType fonts (Korean subset). During `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo`, the only executable code that runs is in the global/top-level scope and any `pkgver()` function.

Key observations:
- The `source` array uses only `file://` URLs for all font files, meaning they reference local files the user must provide. No network downloads (curl/wget/git) occur during source fetching.
- The `DLAGENTS` array is overridden to use `/usr/bin/echo` for `file://` sources, which simply prints a user-friendly message when a file is missing. This is a standard pattern for packages whose sources cannot be legally downloaded from the internet (Microsoft fonts require the user to obtain them separately).
- `sha256sums` contains real checksums for all entries except the final `SKIP`, which is normal practice and explicitly excluded from safety gating.
- There is no `pkgver()` function defined — `pkgver` is set as a plain variable assignment, so no function-body code executes during sourcing.
- No command substitution (`$()`), `eval`, `base64`, or obfuscated code exists in the top-level scope.
- The `_package()` and `package_*()` functions — which contain the actual `install` commands — are NOT executed under `--nobuild` and `--noprepare`, so they are out of scope for this gate.

No genuinely malicious behavior is present. This is consistent with standard AUR packaging practices for a font package whose sources must be obtained manually due to licensing restrictions.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>SAFE: file:// sources, no network, no malicious top-level code</arg_value>
</security_assessment>
